Averaged slacks are averages of nonnegative terms, so tight rows intersect. If a row can be slack at any feasible point, approximate that point by dense targets and project, yielding a strictly slack projected target. This gives decreasing finite contact sets and exact pointwise intersection, including the zero-rank case.

If a row is always tight, dualize max V_z A subject to VA≥c. Nonnegative t has Vᵀt=−V_z and c·t=−c_z; adding a unit weight at z gives an anchored nonnegative zero-gap representation. Conversely a zero-gap representation forces every positively weighted slack to vanish. Vertex decomposition preserves a tight extreme representation using the row. Continuity gives the closed normal sets and Minkowski compatibility plus support equality gives the face inclusion.
